title: Accessory layer — 5 starter accessories on named mount sockets (re-promote of GDP-2026-05-21-005)
intent: Re-file of the accessory layer proposal. S102 notes deferred this because 'joint hierarchy + palette + recipe' had not stabilised. They have now (S102 shipped the 9-pivot tree + 8-channel palette; S103 shipped recipe params + IK + walk cycle). Five starter accessories (antennae / visor / backpack / cap / fins), each mounted on a named pivot socket on the head or torso, painted from existing palette channels, tagged 'soft-attached' for the future spring-sway system. Adds the single largest source of silhouette variety to the bomber. Acceptance hints rewritten against the ACTUAL S102+S103 ECS tree shape — not the original speculative one.
rationale: Source: deferred proposal GDP-2026-05-21-005 (deferred S102, conditions for un-defer met). Plus updated `docs/game-design/characters-and-visual.md` §2.2 — mount sockets are part of the design intent for the post-decomposition tree. The bench currently produces visibly-distinct bombers via palette family (8 options) × proportion knobs (~16 numeric axes). Accessories multiply that diversity by ~8× (5 accessories × 0..3 picked) at marginal performance cost. They are also the lever the cosmetic-unlock plan (gdd.md Cosmetic unlocks) acts on — without accessories there is nothing to unlock. Sequenced after migration (GDP-002 of this batch) because production is where accessory variety actually matters; the bench can preview them but the value lands in-game.
acceptanceHints: Best landed AFTER GDP-2026-05-22-002 (migration) so accessories show up in production from day one — but can also land alongside if dev wants to ship the bench preview first. Either order works; no hard sequencing requirement.
Mount sockets — pivot Object3D entities added to the bomber tree spawner (extends the spawner from S102 PROCBOMBER-MESH-TREE-V0). Always present whether or not any accessory uses them:
head.crown — top of head, position (0, +headSize/2, 0) in head-local space, for antennae + cap
head.eyes — front of head, position (0, 0, +headSize/2 × 0.9) in head-local space, for visor
head.ear.l / head.ear.r — sides of head, for future earphone-style accessories
torso.back — back of torso, position (0, 0, -torsoDepth/2) in torso-local space, for backpack
torso.side.l / torso.side.r — sides of torso, for fins
All 7 sockets are added even when empty (cost ~zero — Transform-only entities). Naming follows the limb-pivot convention from S102: lowercase, dot-suffix.

5 starter accessories. Each is a small node tree under examples/kaboom-crew/src/characters/accessories/<name>.ts (NEW location; lives in kaboom-crew, not bench, because the bench imports from kaboom-crew per GDP-002 of this batch). Each accessory exports a builder that takes recipe.proportions + recipe.palette and returns { rootEntityId, meshes[], pivots[] } via EngineCommand[]:
ANTENNAE — 1..2 thin cylinders (count seed-derived) on head.crown, each topped with a small sphere painted palette.accent (emissive). Length ~0.15 × headSize. Tagged soft-attached.
VISOR — a thin curved box across head.eyes, painted palette.helmet, slightly translucent (material variant opacity ~0.5). Width = headSize × 0.9.

BACKPACK — a rounded box at torso.back, painted palette.torso × 0.85 (use the existing bottom-shadow palette helper from S102). Size 0.4 × 0.35 × 0.15 (W × H × D). NOT soft-attached (backpacks don't sway visibly).
CAP — a cone (8-segment) or hemisphere on head.crown, painted palette.helmet. Optional brim painted palette.head × 0.7 for two-tone read.
FINS — 2 flat triangular meshes on torso.side.l and torso.side.r, painted palette.torsoAccent. Each ~0.25 W × 0.30 H × 0.03 D. Tagged soft-attached.
Recipe surface: `recipe.accessories: ('antennae'|'visor'|'backpack'|'cap'|'fins')[]` — already in the formal schema from GDP-001 of this batch, just needs validator + spawner integration.

Default selection from seed: when recipe.accessories is unspecified, the seed-based resolver from GDP-001 of this batch picks 0..3 deterministically. Weight distribution biased toward 1..2 (rare 0, rare 3). Implementation: derive count from `(seed >> 8) & 3` mapped via weight table [1, 3, 3, 2]; then derive each accessory index by hashing further seed bits, deduplicating.

Soft-attached tag: each soft-attached accessory mesh writes a `SoftAttached` component on its entity (schema entry added to examples/kaboom-crew/schemas/scene-extensions.schema.json). The spring-sway system in GDP-2026-05-22-004 reads this component, no need for the system to traverse the tree.

Palette interaction: accessories paint from existing 8 palette channels. NO new channels added — this is intentional. When cosmetic unlocks ship (future, post-multiplayer), per-channel recipe overrides (already supported via GDP-2026-05-21-003) let an unlock recolour just the cap without touching the rest of the bomber. No accessory-specific palette field is added.

Bench UI: a new 'Accessories' section in the grouped panel (from S103 PROCBOMBER-BENCH-PANEL-SECTIONS). 5 checkboxes (antennae / visor / backpack / cap / fins). Selecting a 4th forces deselection of the oldest. Reroll button respects the seed-based selection distribution.
Production HUD impact: NONE. Accessories are visual-only; no HUD changes, no minimap changes (marker stays driven by palette.head as in GDP-2026-05-22-002).
Determinism: same seed → same accessory set → same mesh tree. Test 200 random seeds, assert no NaN / no duplicates / count distribution matches the weight table.

Visual diversity QA bar: with 5 accessories × 0..3 cardinality and 8 palette families and ~16 numeric axes, the bench/game should produce 50+ visibly distinct bombers in a row before any duplicate-feeling silhouette appears. Manual QA gate, documented in the bench README.

Performance: each accessory adds 1..4 child meshes per bomber. Worst case: 3 accessories × 4 meshes (e.g. cap with brim) = 12 extra meshes per bomber × 4 bombers = 48 accessory draw calls. Combined with body 10 meshes × 4 = 40, total = 88 character draw calls. Still well within the 200-call budget (visual-style.md §11). Bench performance budget unchanged.

Out of scope (explicit): accessory animation independent of the body (the spring-sway in GDP-2026-05-22-004 covers the only motion accessories need), accessory-specific palette channels (deferred per characters-and-visual.md cosmetic-unlock plan), gameplay-affecting accessories (cosmetic-only rule, gdd.md), more accessory types beyond the 5 (deferred — 5 is the design budget for the starter set), Bomb-mesh attached to backpack (future visual flourish; backpack is plain in this story).
